minutes.headline: Water commissioners approved a water rate increase effective January 1, 2023, and OK'd a pilot-study agreement for Hickory Hills well.
minutes.summary: The commissioners discussed and voted a rate increase to cover rising maintenance costs (chemicals, electricity, fuel), with a flyer planned for the January bill. They then moved to have the superintendent sign an engineering agreement with Tighe & Bond for a Hickory Hills well pilot study once counsel approves the legal terms. Other items: PFAS lawsuit, cell tower lease, CDL training idea, and a public comment period that included apologies for a heated prior meeting and a push to post approved minutes online.

public_comment.topic: A Hickory Hills representative apologized for her behavior at the prior meeting, urged commissioners to read the 1994 pumping report, and asked that the Hickory Hills board review the pilot-study scope before a contract is signed.
public_comment.stated_role: Hickory Hills community representative (addressed as Miss Bertram)

public_comment.topic: Woodlands representative clarified that the Woodlands is a separate organization from Hickory Hills landowners and should be contacted directly.
Resident asked about the funding source and contingency for the study money, and whether the scope document would be available to the public.
Resident asked whether Tighe & Bond documents could be handed to the audience at meetings rather than waiting 10 days for a records request.
Asked whether the engineer would attend every meeting and whether that is in their price.
Thanked board, praised the chair's apology, criticized the chaos of the 19th meeting and called for a neutral moderator versed in Robert's Rules.
Introduced as a resident and district member reporting for the Lunenburg Ledger; noted recording the meeting.
Urged posting approved (not draft) minutes on the district web page; board agreed to look into it and likely do it.
Asked whether minutes of the 19th would be verbatim versus the recording.
Praised the moderator at the 19th meeting for handling a difficult situation.

votes.motion: Rate increase to take effect January 1st 2023, with a minimum charge and the second-tier rate per hundred cubic feet as read.
Superintendent to sign the agreement with Tighe & Bond for the scope of work, along with terms and conditions approved by district counsel.

budget_items.what_was_said: Rising electricity, chemicals and fuel costs mean projected maintenance expenses will fall short; the rate increase is meant only to cover this, not future increases.
Staff recommended the higher option with a minimum charge and a per-100-cubic-foot tier, to cover the next two quarters' billing.
Examples were given of current versus new bills at different usage levels, with the average user seeing roughly a monthly increase.
The agreement being signed is a baseline for preliminary planning for the pilot study.
A resident asked if the earlier-voted amount depended on a grant; officials said it comes from service connection fees and the aim is to be better positioned for state funding.
Superintendent described charging for records copies per state rules, with a per-page charge noted.
Bid opening set; bidding expected to save money versus buying off the state list.
Outside CDL schools cost several thousand dollars; an in-house trainer program could avoid that.
The district is part of a class action against PFAS manufacturers; settlement shares might follow flow rates.

decisions.decision: Rate increase effective January 1, 2023 (January billing cycle); a flyer explaining it will go with the January bill.
Form a small contact group with one representative each from Hickory Hills, the Woodlands and the Selectmen for the pilot study scope, with documents emailed ahead of meetings.
District will follow state public records rules (950 CMR) as a procedure in the absence of its own policy.
Board will move to post approved minutes on the district website, bringing it up at the next meeting only if there is a reason not to.
Superintendent to speak with the DPW director about a joint CDL training program.

what_happened.line: Water commissioners voted a rate increase, to take effect January 1, 2023; a flyer explaining it will go out with the January bill.
Commissioners voted to have the superintendent sign an engineering agreement with Tighe & Bond for a Hickory Hills well pilot study, once district counsel approves the terms.
The board agreed to form a small contact group of one representative each from Hickory Hills, the Woodlands and the Selectmen for the pilot study scope.
The board said it will move to post approved minutes on the district website, raising it at the next meeting only if there is a reason not to.
The superintendent will speak with the DPW director about a joint CDL training program, and described the district's part in a PFAS class action.

why_it_matters: Water bills rise from the January 2023 billing cycle; the increase is described as covering higher chemical, electricity and fuel costs, not future increases.

The Hickory Hills well pilot study is paid from service connection fees, and its scope may be shaped by a small group of neighbourhood and town representatives before the engineering contract is signed.
If approved minutes go online, residents will be able to read the board's decisions without a public records request.
